title: Food Transparency
description: BOTIA reads food ingredients and connects what is declared on the label with clear explanations and traceable sources.
home_title_line1: You've read the label a hundred times.
home_title_line2: You still don't know what's in it.
home_description: BOTIA reads the ingredient list for you. It explains what is in the food, in simple words. The explanations are based on scientific evidence. BOTIA does not give the food a score. It does not decide for you.
home_jar_note: A familiar label. More context behind it.
home_how_title: Start with the ingredients. Not the barcode.
home_how_intro: BOTIA uses the ingredient list printed on the package. First it reads the label. Then it explains what it found.
home_step1_body: Take a photo of the label on the product. BOTIA reads the ingredients written on it.
home_step2_body: It finds the ingredients and additives on the label. Then it connects them to the BOTIA layers. Each layer looks at a different question about the food.
home_step3_body: Read the explanation. See what the label can tell you. See what is still uncertain. See the sources behind the information.
home_you_decide: BOTIA shows you what is there. You decide what matters.
home_explore_intro: People read the same label for different reasons. BOTIA keeps each question separate. It does not mix them into one single answer.
home_woman_desc: Evidence about women, when it exists.
home_animal_desc: Ingredients that may come from animals, according to the label.
home_muslim_desc: Halal, haram and doubtful ingredients. The rules used are documented.
home_sugar_desc: Different names and forms of sugars that are easy to miss.
home_sweeteners_desc: Which sweeteners are present and what they are.
home_flavours_desc: What “flavouring” can mean — and what the label may not tell you.
home_texture_desc: Ingredients that give food its texture. For example: emulsifiers, thickeners and stabilisers.
home_enumbers_desc: See which ingredient is behind each E-number code.
home_evidence_desc: See the documentation behind BOTIA's ingredient information.
home_statement_title: BOTIA doesn't tell you what to eat.
home_statement_body: It shows what the label says. It shows what can be known from that. It shows what is still uncertain. It shows the evidence behind the information. The choice is yours.
home_evidence_title: What's in your food — and who says so.
home_evidence_intro: BOTIA links each piece of information to its source. You do not have to trust BOTIA. You can check the source yourself.
home_sources_title: Follow the information back to its source
home_sources_body: Each ingredient page shows where its information comes from. Sources include scientific studies, food authority rules and transparency sources. BOTIA does not hide its reasons behind a score.
home_limits_title: The label has limits. BOTIA keeps them visible.
home_limits_body: If the ingredient list does not reveal origin, manufacturing practice or something that happened before the product reached the shelf, BOTIA should not pretend that it knows.
home_label_limit_title: BOTIA reads the label — not the company behind it.
home_label_limit_body: BOTIA can read what is written on the label. It can explain the ingredients it finds there. It cannot know what the company does. For example, it cannot know about animal testing. It cannot know anything that is not on the label.
home_final_title: Scan the label. See what's there. See the evidence. You decide.
home_final_body: You do not have to believe us. Photograph an ingredient list. See what BOTIA finds.
footer_try_desc: Photograph the label. Discover what it doesn't say.
footer_disclaimer: BOTIA does not replace the official health and food authorities. For example: WHO, EFSA, the European Commission and the FDA. It does not replace scientific studies either. BOTIA turns complex food evidence into simple information. You can use it while you read a label.
home_nutrition_desc: Nutrition values from the label, plus official reference values.
robot_answers: Because a barcode identifies a product but does not explain its formulation. BOTIA starts with the actual ingredients list because it shows what the manufacturer declares that food contains.

Because a single score would mix different questions and hide what cannot be known from the label. BOTIA separates what is declared, what can be identified, what is uncertain and the evidence supporting it.

Because the same list can matter for nutritional, religious or ethical reasons, or because of animal origin, pregnancy or exposure. BOTIA keeps these questions separate rather than reducing them to one answer.
